haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine writes its invoices to the shadow store only, never charging or writing the ledger.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store without charging.
haiku-low.q3: Gate A must be met: 7 consecutive nights under 0.1% mismatch and at least 5,000 invoices compared. A person makes the promotion request.
haiku-low.q4: The charge-failure monitor's auto-trigger starts it when failures exceed 2% in 10 minutes, in both or new_only. On-call can also start it manually from shadow, both or new_only.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only. Gates reset and the 7-day count restarts. The rollout must go through shadow again before new_only.
haiku-low.q6: It stops at day 35 in new_only, counted from entering new_only. Old-engine skipped events begin expiring from the 35-day usage log then, so rollback must start before day 35.
haiku-low.q7: NOT STATED for the polling or push mechanism. An in-flight charge is protected by the ledger key, so at most one charge per period happens.
haiku-low.q8: Nightly result rows are read by the controller, which updates gate counters in the rollout record. The controller refuses a promotion whose gate is not met.
haiku-low.q9: The charge-failure monitor measures failed charge attempts divided by all attempts over a sliding 10-minute window. Above 2%, it sends the controller a rollback request and pages on-call.
haiku-low.q10: Workers do not charge while the fence is set, so due periods stay due and uncharged. They are charged after step 6 flips the flag to old_only and clears the fence.
haiku-low.q11: The ledger key, customer plus billing period, makes a second charge for the same period a no-op whichever engine attempts it. Step 5 pages on-call if a double charge is found.
haiku-low.q12: Billing stays safe: fence set, flag unchanged, charges delayed. The failed step is retried and on-call paged. The flag flips only after verification passes.

sonnet.q1: The old engine computes, writes the ledger and charges. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes invoices to the shadow store only. It never charges and never writes the ledger.
sonnet.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store without charging. It skips no events, so its checkpoint stays current.
sonnet.q3: The current mode must be shadow, no rollback may be running, the rollout record must show no half-finished promotion, and gate A must be met. Gate A is 7 consecutive days, each with a nightly mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared in total. A person makes the move. Meeting the gate does not trigger it.
sonnet.q4: The charge-failure monitor (auto-trigger) starts it when failed charge attempts divided by all attempts exceed 2% over a sliding 10-minute window. This only applies in `both` or `new_only`. It sends the controller a rollback request and pages on-call. In new_only on day 35 or later the controller refuses the request.
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in `old_only`. The gates are reset, so the 7-day count restarts, and the 14-day count and comparison history also start over. The rollout must then go through `shadow` again and meet gate A, then gate B with Finance sign-off, before reaching new_only. Each promotion is made by a person.
sonnet.q6: A rollback must start before day 35, counted from when new_only was entered. On day 35 or later the controller refuses it, changes nothing and pages on-call, who fix forward. The reason is that on day 35 the oldest events the old engine skipped start to expire from the 35-day usage event log. A rollback already running on day 35 finishes, because it pinned its events.
sonnet.q7: Workers read the `billing_mode` flag and the fence key from the config service. How they read them (polling or push) and the maximum staleness are not decided (open question 7). Retirement is the exception: it does not change the flag. NOT STATED for what happens to an invoice being processed at the moment of a normal promotion. For a rollback, in-flight charges are settled in step 2, and the ledger key prevents double charges even if a worker's view is stale.
sonnet.q8: The nightly comparison job writes one result row per night. The controller reads those rows and updates the gate counters in the rollout record. The Finance sign-off is also stored in the rollout record, and gate B reads it from there. The controller checks the gate itself and refuses a promotion request, with the reason, if the gate is not met. The mode must also be the step just before the requested one, no rollback may be running, and there must be no half-finished promotion. Promotions are made only by a person.
sonnet.q9: The auto-trigger, a charge-failure monitor still to be built. It reads the charge results that workers record in the billing ledger. It measures failed charge attempts divided by all attempts (retries included) over a sliding 10-minute window, only in `both` or `new_only`. When the rate is above 2% it sends the controller a rollback request and pages on-call. If there are no attempts in the window, nothing triggers.
sonnet.q10: Charges that fall due while a rollback is running are not made and not dropped. Workers do not charge while the fence is set, so a period that falls due stays due and uncharged in the ledger. They are charged after step 6, when the flag is set to old_only and then the fence is cleared. The old engine's normal run then recomputes each due period with no `charged` entry from the usage events and charges it. That assumption is unverified. From shadow there is no fence, and the old engine keeps charging throughout.
sonnet.q11: The ledger key (customer plus billing period) stops it. Workers write it as `attempting` before calling the provider and pass the same key as the provider's idempotency key. A second charge for the same period is then a no-op, whichever engine attempts it. Only a `charged` entry counts as a charge, so reprocessing skips periods already `charged`. Step 5 also checks that each due period has exactly one `charged` entry. If two are found, on-call is paged to fix it by hand.
sonnet.q12: Billing is left in a safe state. The fence stays set, the flag is unchanged, and charges are delayed but never dropped or duplicated. The controller retries the failed step and pages on-call. The flag does not flip until verification passes. If the controller crashes, it resumes from the current step stored in the rollout record, and the step 1 wait is not restarted because the fence write time is stored.
